name: Johor
summary_text: Worse than national — a state-funded conversion infrastructure. Singapore's commuter twin, the country's most cosmopolitan Malay-majority city (Johor Bahru), directly across the border from a wealthy city-state. In February 2025 the state established an RM400,000 centre to 'rehabilitate' members of deviant groups and people in same-sex relationships, described by the state Islamic religious affairs committee chairman as for individuals with 'distorted' beliefs and those convicted by the syariah court for same-sex relationships, 'to help them resume a normal life'. Independent ethnographic research documents how trans women across the country are channelled into state and religious-institution 'moral reform' programmes aimed at 'rehabilitating' LGBTQ+ Muslims — the rehabilitation apparatus is real, funded, and reaches trans women specifically. Scored relative to the national score (0.16) for Malaysia.

sources.title: Malaysia: State-Backed Discrimination Harms LGBT People | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch dispatch (10 August 2022), 'State-Backed Discrimination Harms LGBT People in Malaysia': national analysis of religious authorities and state agencies driving anti-LGBT discrimination, including the 2021 Nur Sajat manhunt by another state's religious department — the enforcement channel of the kind this state's apparatus also runs.

sources.title: “The Deceased Can’t Speak for Herself:” Violence Against LGBT People in Malaysia | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report (25 June 2019), "Deceased Can't Speak for Herself: Violence Against LGBT People in Malaysia": investigation of killings and violence against LGBT people in the country and the failures of investigation and justice in those cases, establishing the national violence-and-impunity pattern relevant to every state including this one.
